newsitem.title: USA: PacifiCorp tries to keep Big River partner.
newsitem.headline: PacifiCorp tries to keep Big River partner.

text.p: PacifiCorp said Thursday it had asked a district court to take jurisdiction over the reorganization of Big Rivers Electric Corp away from bankruptcy court in an effort to halt a legal battle and preserve its partnership with the utility.
The company said it had asked the U.S. District Court to take jurisdiction over the reorganization of the financially-troubled utility away from the U.S. Bankruptcy Court.
It said it also filed motions in bankruptcy court requesting that the judge remove himself and the bankruptcy examiner from the case and impose sanctions on the examiner.
"The auction process decreed by (the judge) last week was improper because Schilling had contacts with the judge that are prohibited by federal bankruptcy court rules," it said.

The process caused "great harm" to the efforts of the utility's major creditors and customers to resolve its financial troubles, it said, adding that the creditors had agreed to a settlement of the utility's bankruptcy when the judge reversed his decision to see a negotiated settlement.
PacifiCorp became partner of Big Rivers more than 14 months ago.
On February 10, LG&E Energy Corp offered to lease or acquire the utility.

The Big Rivers-PacifiCorp partnership provides for PacifiCorp to lease and operate Big Rivers generation facilities over the next 25 years for an annual payment of $30.1 million. PacifiCorp will sell power back to Big Rivers for use by its four distribution cooperative members and sell the surplus into the eastern wholesale power markets.
